### 6. Equation for the error and mean curvature approximation by Toda system

We derive the equation satisfied by the error function $\phi$ defined in (5.114), and then project this equation onto $\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}$ to obtain the Toda system. We use the geometric estimates of Section 4, the heteroclinic estimates in Section 5, and the optimal shifts of Proposition 5.7. In particular, the shifts are $o(1)$ in $C^{3,\theta}$ as in Remark 5.8.

$B_{s}^{+}(y,z)$ denotes the ambient coordinate ball $B_{s}^{+}(Y_{\Sigma_{\alpha}}(y,z))$ , intersected with the half-domain. A sheet ball $B_{s}^{\alpha}(y)$ is the coordinate ball on $\Sigma_{\alpha}$ defined in Section 5. We identify a base point $y\in\Sigma_{\alpha}$ with the ambient point $Y_{\Sigma_{\alpha}}(y,0)$ .

#### 6.1. Equation for the error $\phi$

The following computation is the counterpart of [29, (4.11)], with the boundary correction and the twisted-coordinate terms retained.

#### Proposition 6.1.

In the $\alpha$ -coordinates, the error satisfies

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\Delta_{\alpha,z}\phi-&H_{\alpha}(y,z)\partial_{z}\phi+\partial_{zz}\phi+\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}\phi\\
&={}W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*}+\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)-\sum_{\beta}W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})-\sum_{\beta}W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})\mathbb{G}_{\beta}\\
&\quad+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}\bigl(H_{\alpha}(y,z)+\Delta_{\alpha,z}h_{\alpha}\bigr)-\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\alpha}|\nabla_{\alpha,z}h_{\alpha}|^{2}\\
&\quad+\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}\bigl[(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}-\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}\bigr]\\
&\quad-\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}-\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta},\end{split} $$

where $\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}(y,z)$ is the second order linear differential operator defined in (4.65), $H_{\alpha}(y,z)$ is the mean curvature of $\Sigma_{\alpha,z}$ (cf. Proposition 4.19), and

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\xi_{\beta}(y,z)={}&\bar{\xi}_{1}\bigl((-1)^{\beta}(z-h_{\beta}(y))\bigr)+\bar{\xi}_{2,\beta}\bigl(y,(-1)^{\beta}(z-h_{\beta}(y))\bigr),\\
\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}(y,z)={}&H_{\beta}(y,z)+\Delta_{\beta,z}h_{\beta}(y),\\
\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}(y,z)={}&|\nabla_{\beta,z}h_{\beta}(y)|^{2},\\
\mathcal{R}_{\beta,3}(y,z)={}&-2(-1)^{\beta}\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}g_{\beta}^{ij}(y,z)\mathbb{G}^{\prime}_{\beta,i}(y,z)\partial_{y_{j}}h_{\beta}(y),\\
\mathcal{R}_{\beta,4}(y,z)={}&\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}\bigl(g_{\beta}^{ij}(y,z)-g_{\beta}^{ij}(y,0)\bigr)\mathbb{G}_{\beta,ij}(y,z)\\
&-\sum_{i,j,k=1}^{n}\bigl(g_{\beta}^{ij}(y,z)\Gamma^{k}_{\beta,ij}(y,z)-g_{\beta}^{ij}(y,0)\Gamma^{k}_{\beta,ij}(y,0)\bigr)\mathbb{G}_{\beta,k}(y,z).\end{split} $$

The correction terms are

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\mathcal{G}_{\beta}\ &=\mathcal{G}_{\beta,1}+\mathcal{G}_{\beta,2}+\mathcal{G}_{\beta,3}+\mathcal{G}_{\beta,4}+\mathcal{G}_{\beta,5},\\
\mathcal{G}_{\beta,1}&=(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{G}^{\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1},\\
\mathcal{G}_{\beta,2}&=-\mathbb{G}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2},\\
\mathcal{G}_{\beta,3}&=-\mathcal{R}_{\beta,3},\\
\mathcal{G}_{\beta,4}&=-\mathcal{R}_{\beta,4},\\
\mathcal{G}_{\beta,5}&=-\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{G}_{\beta}.\end{split} $$

At every base point to which Proposition 5.7 applies, one also has

$$ \int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi(y,z)\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}(y,z)\,dz=0. $$

#### Proof.

In twisted Fermi coordinates with respect to $\Sigma_{\beta}$ , one has $\widetilde{Z}=\partial_{z}-\sum_{i}T^{i}\partial_{y_{i}}$ . Expanding $\Delta=\Delta_{\beta,z}+\widetilde{Z}^{2}-H_{\beta}\widetilde{Z}$ gives

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\phi={}&-2\sum_{i}T^{i}\partial_{y_{i}z}\phi+\sum_{i,j}T^{i}T^{j}\partial_{y_{i}y_{j}}\phi+\sum_{j}\Bigl(\sum_{i}T^{i}\partial_{y_{i}}T^{j}-\partial_{z}T^{j}+H_{\beta}T^{j}\Bigr)\partial_{y_{j}}\phi.\end{split} $$

and the coefficients can be estimated by (4.47). The chain rule gives

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\partial_{y_{i}}\mathbb{G}_{\beta}&=\mathbb{G}_{\beta,i}-(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{G}^{\prime}_{\beta}\partial_{y_{i}}h_{\beta},\\
\partial_{y_{i}y_{j}}\mathbb{G}_{\beta}&=\mathbb{G}_{\beta,ij}-(-1)^{\beta}\bigl(\mathbb{G}^{\prime}_{\beta,i}\partial_{y_{j}}h_{\beta}+\mathbb{G}^{\prime}_{\beta,j}\partial_{y_{i}}h_{\beta}+\mathbb{G}^{\prime}_{\beta}\partial_{y_{i}y_{j}}h_{\beta}\bigr)\\
&\qquad+\mathbb{G}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}\partial_{y_{i}}h_{\beta}\partial_{y_{j}}h_{\beta},\\
\partial_{z}\mathbb{G}_{\beta}&=(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{G}^{\prime}_{\beta},\qquad\partial_{zz}\mathbb{G}_{\beta}=\mathbb{G}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}.\end{split} $$

After contraction with $g_{\beta}^{ij}(y,z)$ , the two terms containing $\mathbb{G}^{\prime}_{\beta,i}\partial_{y_{j}}h_{\beta}$ give $\mathcal{R}_{\beta,3}$ , while the difference between the first-argument Laplacians at heights $z$ and $0$ is $\mathcal{R}_{\beta,4}$ . Hence the equation for $\bar{\mathbb{G}}_{\beta}$ in (5.14) becomes

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\Delta\mathbb{G}_{\beta}={}&W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})\mathbb{G}_{\beta}+\xi_{2,\beta}-(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{G}^{\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}+\mathbb{G}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}\\
&+\mathcal{R}_{\beta,3}+\mathcal{R}_{\beta,4}+\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{G}_{\beta}.\end{split} $$

For the heteroclinic, we have

$$ \partial_{y_{i}}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}=-(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}\partial_{y_{i}}h_{\beta},\qquad\partial_{y_{i}y_{j}}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}=\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}\partial_{y_{i}}h_{\beta}\partial_{y_{j}}h_{\beta}-(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}\partial_{y_{i}y_{j}}h_{\beta}. $$

Since $\partial_{z}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}=(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}$ and $\partial_{zz}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}=\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}$ , we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\Delta\mathbb{H}_{\beta}={}&W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})+\bar{\xi}_{1}\bigl((-1)^{\beta}(z-h_{\beta}(y))\bigr)\\
&-(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}+\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}+\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}.\end{split} $$

Finally, by the Allen–Cahn equation

$$ \Delta u=W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*}+\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi). $$

Subtracting the sum of (6.8) and (6.7) from (6.9) gives (6.1). Finally, (6.4) is (5.42). ∎

The nonlinear terms admit the following exact decomposition

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}W^{\prime}(u)-\sum_{\beta}W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})-\sum_{\beta}W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})\mathbb{G}_{\beta}=W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi+\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)+\mathcal{I}_{1}+\mathcal{I}_{2},\end{split} $$

where

$$ \mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)=W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*}+\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)-W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi), $$

$$ \mathcal{I}_{1}=W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-\sum_{\beta}W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta}), $$

and

$$ \mathcal{I}_{2}=\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{I}_{2,\beta}=\sum_{\beta}\bigl(W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})\bigr)\mathbb{G}_{\beta}. $$

Moreover, by Taylor’s formula

$$ \mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)=(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)^{2}\int_{0}^{1}(1-t)W^{\prime\prime\prime}\bigl(\mathbb{H}_{*}+t(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)\bigr)\,dt. $$

The sums $\mathbb{H}_{*}$ and $\mathbb{G}_{*}$ have uniform $C^{2,\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(p))$ bounds for $p\in B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$ , by exponential decay and separation of the sheets. Interior and Neumann estimates for $u$ on $B_{2}^{+}(p)$ give the same bound for $u$ , and hence for $\phi$ , on $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ . Hence,

$$ \|\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)\|_{C^{k,\theta}(\Omega)}\leq C\bigl(\|\mathbb{G}_{*}\|_{C^{k,\theta}(\Omega)}^{2}+\|\phi\|_{C^{k,\theta}(\Omega)}^{2}\bigr),\quad k=0,1,2. $$

Constants in these estimates do not depend on the number of sheets.

#### Lemma 6.2 (Interaction terms).

For $(y,z)\in\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{4}\cap B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$ ,

$$ |\mathcal{I}_{1}(y,z)|\leq C\bigl(e^{-D_{\alpha}(y)}+\varepsilon^{2}\bigr), $$

$$ |\mathcal{I}_{2}(y,z)|\leq C\bigl(e^{-3D_{\alpha}(y)/2}+\varepsilon^{2}\bigr). $$

For $(y,z)\in\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{3}\cap B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$ , the corresponding norm estimates are

$$ \displaystyle\|\mathcal{I}_{1}\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))} \displaystyle\leq C\|\mathcal{I}_{1}\|_{\mathrm{Lip}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))}\lesssim\sup_{B_{2}^{\alpha}(y)}e^{-D_{\alpha}}+\varepsilon^{2}, \displaystyle\|\mathcal{I}_{2}\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))} \displaystyle\leq C\|\mathcal{I}_{2}\|_{\mathrm{Lip}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))}\lesssim\sup_{B_{2}^{\alpha}(y)}e^{-3D_{\alpha}/2}+\varepsilon^{2}. $$

#### Proof.

The proof follows the interaction estimates in [29, Section 4.2]. By Proposition 4.25, separation, and Lemma 4.30, we have

$$ \sum_{\beta:\,|t_{\beta}(x)|\leq 10|\log\varepsilon|}e^{-\sigma|t_{\beta}(x)|}\leq C_{\sigma}\qquad(\sigma>0). $$

The same geometric-series argument bounds the sum over $|t_{\beta}(x)|>s$ by $C_{\sigma}e^{-\sigma s}$ . On $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{\lambda}$ , the sum over all the sheets $\beta\neq\alpha$ is bounded by $C_{\sigma}e^{-\sigma|z|}$ .

Let us begin with the term $\mathcal{I}_{1}=W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-\sum_{\beta}W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})$ . For $\beta\neq\alpha$ , exponential decay gives

$$ \displaystyle|\mathbb{H}_{\beta}-\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha-\beta)(-1)^{\beta}|+|\nabla\mathbb{H}_{\beta}| \displaystyle\leq Ce^{-|t_{\beta}|}, \displaystyle|W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha})-1|+|\nabla W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha})| \displaystyle\leq Ce^{-|z|}. $$

Hence, Taylor expansion using $W^{\prime}(\pm 1)=0$ and $W^{\prime\prime}(\pm 1)=1$ yields

$$ \begin{split}\mathcal{I}_{1}={}&[W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha})-1]\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}[\mathbb{H}_{\beta}-\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha-\beta)(-1)^{\beta}]+O\Bigl(\bigl(\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}e^{-|t_{\beta}|}\bigr)^{2}\Bigr).\end{split} $$

Differentiating the integral Taylor remainder and using (6.20) gives the same quadratic bound for the first derivatives. Hence

$$ |\mathcal{I}_{1}|+|\nabla\mathcal{I}_{1}|\leq Ce^{-|z|}\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}e^{-|t_{\beta}|}. $$

The terms with $|t_{\beta}|>2|\log\varepsilon|$ sum to $O(\varepsilon^{2})$ . For the other indices, Proposition 4.25 gives $|z|+|t_{\beta}(y,z)|\geq|t_{\beta}(y,0)|-o(1)$ . Summing these contributions proves (6.15).

For $\mathcal{I}_{2}=\sum_{\beta}[W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})]\mathbb{G}_{\beta}$ , let us first separate the $\alpha$ -sheet contribution from the contributions of the other sheets.

For the $\alpha$ sheet, by Taylor expansion,

$$ |W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha})|+|\nabla(W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}))|\leq C\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}e^{-|t_{\beta}|}, $$

while for $\beta\neq\alpha$ ,

$$ |W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})-1|+|\nabla W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})|\leq Ce^{-|t_{\beta}|}. $$

Combining these inequalities with Corollary 5.10, for any fixed $\sigma\in[3/4,1)$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}|\mathcal{I}_{2}|+|\nabla\mathcal{I}_{2}|&\leq C_{\sigma}\varepsilon\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}\bigl(e^{-\sigma|z|-|t_{\beta}|}+e^{-|z|-\sigma|t_{\beta}|}\bigr)\leq C_{\sigma}\varepsilon\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}e^{-\sigma(|z|+|t_{\beta}|)}.\end{split} $$

The second inequality uses the preceding distance splitting; the last is Young’s inequality. This proves (6.16).

If either distance is larger than $2|\log\varepsilon|$ , then

$$ C_{\sigma}\varepsilon e^{-2\sigma|\log\varepsilon|}=C_{\sigma}\varepsilon^{1+2\sigma}\leq C_{\sigma}\varepsilon^{2}. $$

Otherwise the distance comparison and Lemma 4.30 give

$$ C_{\sigma}\varepsilon\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}e^{-\sigma|t_{\beta}(y,0)|}\leq C_{\sigma}\varepsilon e^{-\sigma D_{\alpha}(y)}\leq C_{\sigma}\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+e^{-2\sigma D_{\alpha}(y)}\bigr). $$

Taking $\sigma=3/4$ proves (6.16) and its first-derivative analogue.

Fix $p=Y_{\Sigma_{\alpha}}(y,z)\in\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{3}\cap B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$ . Then $B_{1}^{+}(p)\subset\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{6}$ and $\Pi_{\alpha}(B_{1}^{+}(p))\subset B_{2}^{\alpha}(y)$ . Apply the preceding pointwise and first-derivative estimates at the points of $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ , taking the supremum of $e^{-D_{\alpha}}$ and $e^{-3D_{\alpha}/2}$ on $B_{2}^{\alpha}(y)$ . The Lipschitz bound on $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ controls its $C^{\theta}$ norm and proves (6.17) and (6.18). ∎

#### Lemma 6.3.

Let $(y,z)\in B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$ . Then

$$ \Bigl\|\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}\Bigr\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))}\leq C\varepsilon^{3}. $$

For $|z|\leq 9|\log\varepsilon|$ one has

$$ \displaystyle\|\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}\phi\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))} \displaystyle\leq C\varepsilon(1+|z|^{2})\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))} \displaystyle\leq C\varepsilon^{2}(1+|z|^{4})+C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))}^{2}. $$

The other geometric and correction terms satisfy

$$ \displaystyle\Bigl\|\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}\Bigr\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))} \displaystyle\leq C\varepsilon\max_{\beta:\,|t_{\beta}(y,z)|\leq 10|\log\varepsilon|}\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{2}^{\beta}(\Pi_{\beta}(y,z)))}+C\varepsilon^{2}, \displaystyle\Bigl\|\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta}\Bigr\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))} \displaystyle\leq C\varepsilon\max_{\beta:\,|t_{\beta}(y,z)|\leq 10|\log\varepsilon|}\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{2}^{\beta}(\Pi_{\beta}(y,z)))}+C\varepsilon^{2}. $$

#### Proof.

We estimate the four expressions in the order in which they occur in the statement.

First, by (5.4) and (5.17), we have

$$ \|\xi_{\beta}\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))}\leq C\varepsilon^{3}e^{-|t_{\beta}(y,z)|/4}, $$

and summing with (6.19) proves (6.28).

Next, on $|z|\leq 9|\log\varepsilon|$ , the coefficients in (6.5), together with their local $C^{\theta}$ norms, are bounded by $C\varepsilon(1+|z|^{2})$ , so the product estimate gives the first line of (6.29); Young’s inequality gives the second line.

For (6.30), the proof proceeds as in the previous paragraph. We compute

$$ \displaystyle\Bigl|\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}(y,z)(\mathbb{H}_{\beta})\Bigr| \displaystyle\lesssim\sum_{\beta}e^{-|t_{\beta}(y,z)|}[\varepsilon|z|(|\nabla^{2}_{\beta}h_{\beta}|+|\nabla_{\beta}h_{\beta}|)] \displaystyle\lesssim\varepsilon\max_{\beta:|t_{\beta}(y,0)|<8|\log\varepsilon|}(|\nabla^{2}_{\beta}h_{\beta}|+|\nabla_{\beta}h_{\beta}|)+\varepsilon^{2}, $$

where we appealed to (4.94) and (4.102) to estimate $D\Pi_{\beta}$ and to control the exponential sum. The $C^{\theta}$ -Hölder norm estimate follows in a similar way.

Finally, to prove (6.31), we estimate the five terms in (6.3) before summing them. Notice that their $C^{\theta}$ norms are bounded respectively by

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|\mathcal{G}_{\beta,1}\|_{C^{\theta}}&\leq C_{\sigma}\varepsilon e^{-\sigma|z|}\bigl(\varepsilon+\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{2,\theta}}\bigr),\\
\|\mathcal{G}_{\beta,2}\|_{C^{\theta}}&\leq C_{\sigma}\varepsilon e^{-\sigma|z|}\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^{2},\\
\|\mathcal{G}_{\beta,3}\|_{C^{\theta}}&\leq C_{\sigma}\varepsilon e^{-\sigma|z|}\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{1,\theta}},\\
\|\mathcal{G}_{\beta,4}\|_{C^{\theta}}+\|\mathcal{G}_{\beta,5}\|_{C^{\theta}}&\leq C_{\sigma}\varepsilon^{2}e^{-\sigma|z|},\end{split} $$

where the first line uses $H_{\beta}=O(\varepsilon)$ ; the second uses $\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}=|\nabla_{\beta,z}h_{\beta}|^{2}$ ; and the third is the explicit term $\mathcal{R}_{\beta,3}$ in (6.2). For the fourth line, the coefficients in $\mathcal{R}_{\beta,4}$ are $O(\varepsilon(1+|z|^{2}))$ in $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\theta}$ , while the derivatives of $\bar{\mathbb{G}}_{\beta}$ are $O(\varepsilon e^{-\sigma|z|})$ . The same reasoning applies to $\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{G}_{\beta}$ , using (6.6). Summing (6.34) by (6.19) proves (6.31). ∎

#### 6.2. Mean curvature and the Toda system with rough error

Substituting (6.10) into (6.1) gives

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\Delta_{\alpha,z}\phi-H_{\alpha}\partial_{z}\phi+\partial_{zz}\phi={}&W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi+\mathcal{I}_{1}+\mathcal{I}_{2}+\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)\\
&+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}(H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,z}h_{\alpha})-\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\alpha}|\nabla_{\alpha,z}h_{\alpha}|^{2}\\
&+\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}\bigl[(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}-\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}\bigr]-\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}\\
&-\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}\phi-\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta},\end{split} $$

where the estimates for $\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*})$ , $\mathcal{I}_{1}$ , $\mathcal{I}_{2}$ and the last four terms are given in (6.14), Lemma 6.2 and Lemma 6.3.

We can now derive the Toda system satisfied by the layer distances.

#### Proposition 6.4 (Toda system).

For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ , on $\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$ ,

$$ H_{\alpha}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}(y)=\frac{2}{\sigma_{0}}\bigl(A_{(-1)^{\alpha-1}}^{2}e^{-|t_{\alpha-1}(y,0)|}-A_{(-1)^{\alpha}}^{2}e^{-|t_{\alpha+1}(y,0)|}\bigr)+E_{\alpha}^{0}(y). $$

Here $A_{\pm 1}$ are defined in (C.2). For every $x\in B^{+}_{6R/7}(0)$ and $0<r<R/60$ , the remainder satisfies

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\max_{\alpha}\|E_{\alpha}^{0}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\lesssim{}&\varepsilon^{2}+\varepsilon^{1/3}A(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)+A(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/2}\\
&+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}\\
&+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}.\end{split} $$

#### Proof.

Fix $x\in B^{+}_{6R/7}(0)$ and $0<r<R/60$ . Differentiating (6.4) twice and taking the horizontal trace gives

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Delta_{\alpha,0}\phi\,\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}\,dz={}&(-1)^{\alpha}\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\alpha}\,dz-|\nabla_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}|^{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime\prime}_{\alpha}\,dz\\
&+2(-1)^{\alpha}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\langle\nabla_{\alpha,0}\phi,\nabla_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\rangle\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\alpha}\,dz.\end{split} $$

Multiply (6.35) by $\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}$ and integrate in $z$ with respect to $dz$ . The identity $\bar{\mathbb{H}}^{\prime\prime\prime}=W^{\prime\prime}(\bar{\mathbb{H}})\bar{\mathbb{H}}^{\prime}+\bar{\xi}^{\prime}_{1}$ cancels the principal normal term, up to the cutoff error.

Now set

$$ \mathbf{E}_{\alpha}(y)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\bigl[\mathcal{I}_{2}+\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)-\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}\phi-\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta}\bigr]\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}\,dz. $$

Lemmas 6.2 and 6.3, (6.14), and the correction bounds in Corollary 5.10 give

$$ \max_{\alpha}\|\mathbf{E}_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/2}+C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}. $$

Then, we estimate the remaining terms as in [29, proof of Lemma 5.1], using Proposition 4.19 and Lemma 5.12 . In particular, for the $\beta\neq\alpha$ curvature terms, retain $H_{\beta}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}$ as a single $C^{\theta}$ factor and bound the overlap using

$$ \int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{-|z|-|z+t|}\,dz=(1+|t|)e^{-|t|}\leq Ce^{-3|t|/4}. $$

Together with the distance comparison and exponential summability, this bounds their contribution by a constant times $A(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/4}$ multiplied by $\max_{\beta}\|H_{\beta}+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}\|_{C^{\theta}}$ . The potential-difference term is bounded in the same way, with the curvature norm replaced by $\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}$ . Young’s inequality, the cutoff estimates, and (6.40) therefore give

$$ \displaystyle\max_{\alpha}\Bigl\|(-1)^{\alpha}(H_{\alpha}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha})\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha})^{2}\,dz+\int_{\mathbb{R}}\mathcal{I}_{1}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}\,dz\Bigr\|_{C^{\theta}} \displaystyle\qquad\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/2}+C\max_{\beta}\|H_{\beta}+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}\|_{C^{\theta}}^{2}+C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^{2}. $$

All these estimates hold in $C^{\theta}$ .

In order to estimate the leading interaction, we use the decomposition in [29, Lemma B.1], where only the two adjacent linear tails contribute at leading order. The quadratic tails contribute $CA(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/2}$ , while nonadjacent tails contribute $CA(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{2}$ . On the common logarithmic strips, the estimates of Section 4 give $t_{\beta}(\cdot,z)-t_{\beta}(\cdot,0)-z=O_{C^{1}}(\varepsilon^{1/3})$ ; the first-derivative bound follows by differentiating along the twisted flow. We can then proceed as in [29, Lemma 5.1]. Using (C.2) gives

$$ \displaystyle\max_{\alpha}\left\|\int_{\mathbb{R}}\mathcal{I}_{1}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}\,dz+2(-1)^{\alpha}\left(A_{(-1)^{\alpha-1}}^{2}e^{-|t_{\alpha-1}(\cdot,0)|}-A_{(-1)^{\alpha}}^{2}e^{-|t_{\alpha+1}(\cdot,0)|}\right)\right\|_{C^{\theta}} \displaystyle\qquad\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+C\varepsilon^{1/3}A(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)+CA(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/2}+C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^{2}. $$

Finally, $\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha})^{2}\,dz=\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\bar{\mathbb{H}}^{\prime})^{2}\,dz=\sigma_{0}+O(\varepsilon^{3})$ , independently of $y$ and $\alpha$ . Combining (6.41) and (6.42), dividing by this positive mass and by $(-1)^{\alpha}$ , and using $A^{2}\leq A^{3/2}$ for $0\leq A\leq 1$ , proves (6.36) with the remainder estimate (6.37). ∎

#### Corollary 6.5.

For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ , every $x\in B^{+}_{6R/7}(0)$ and $0<r<R/60$ satisfy

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\\
&\quad\leq\frac{1}{4}\bigl[\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}\bigr]\\
&\qquad\quad+C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x).\end{split} $$

#### Proof.

The mean value theorem and the uniform bound for the tangential derivatives of the distance functions give

$$ \|e^{-|t_{\alpha\pm 1}(\cdot,0)|}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\leq CA(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x). $$

Combining this with (6.36)-(6.37) gives

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)\\
&\qquad+C\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}+C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}.\end{split} $$

Since $H_{\alpha}=O(\varepsilon)$ in $C^{\theta}$ and $h_{\alpha}=o(1)$ in $C^{3,\theta}$ , the $C^{\theta}$ norm of $H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}$ on $B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))$ is $o(1)$ uniformly, therefore we can absorb it and obtain (6.43). ∎

### 7. Inner-outer gluing estimates for the error function $\phi$

We estimate the error $\phi=u-\mathbb{H}_{*}-\mathbb{G}_{*}$ by combining the equation and the orthogonality condition obtained in Section 6. The argument follows the inner–outer decomposition of [29, Section 6]. At the boundary, however, the approximate solution has nonzero Neumann derivative, which we shall estimate in Section 7.1.

#### Proposition 7.1 ( $C^{2,\theta}$ estimates).

For every fixed $\theta\in(0,1)$ there are $\varepsilon_{0}>0$ and $C<\infty$ , depending only on the standing data and $\theta$ , such that, whenever $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_{0}$ , $x\in B^{+}_{6R/7}(0)$ and $0<r<R/60$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))}+\max_{\alpha}\|h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{2,\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\\
&\qquad+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+100|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x).\end{split} $$

The constants are independent of the number of sheets.

We shall use the following qualitative smallness statement

$$ \begin{split}&\|\varphi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0))}+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0))}=o(1)\quad\text{as }\varepsilon\to 0,\end{split} $$

which follows from Lemma 4.30, Lemma 4.31, (5.116), and the fact that $H_{\alpha}=O(\varepsilon)$ in $C^{\theta}$ and $h_{\alpha}=o(1)$ in $C^{3,\theta}$ (see [29, Remark 4.2]).

#### 7.1. Neumann derivative estimates for $\phi$

#### Proposition 7.2 (Neumann derivative estimate).

For each ambient ball $B_{r}^{+}(x)$ used in this section, with $B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x)\subset B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\|\partial_{\nu}\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(\partial_{0}B_{r}^{+}(x))} \displaystyle\lesssim\varepsilon^{2}+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}+A(r+80|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/2}. $$

#### Proof.

We first compute the contribution of one sheet in its own coordinates. Set

$$ N^{\beta}=\partial_{\nu}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\mathbb{G}_{\beta}),\qquad-\partial_{\nu}\phi=\sum_{\beta}N^{\beta}. $$

By (5.20), we have the exact formula

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}N^{\beta}(y,z)={}&(-1)^{\beta}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}+\mathbb{G}_{\beta}^{\prime})\bigl(J_{\beta}-\sum_{j=1}^{n}(\partial_{y_{j}}h_{\beta})\,\partial_{\nu}y_{j}\bigr)+\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbb{G}_{\beta,j}\,\partial_{\nu}y_{j}.\end{split} $$

By definition of $\mathbb{G}_{\beta,1}$ and (5.14), we have

$$ \mathbb{G}_{\beta,1}(y,z)=-(-1)^{\beta}w_{\beta}(y)(z-h_{\beta}(y))\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}(y,z)+\delta_{\beta}\bigl(y,(-1)^{\beta}(z-h_{\beta}(y))\bigr). $$

Substituting this and $J_{\beta}=w_{\beta}z+\widetilde{J}_{\beta}$ into (7.5) yields

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}N^{\beta}={}&(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}\bigl(\widetilde{J}_{\beta}+w_{\beta}h_{\beta}-\partial_{y_{1}}h_{\beta}\bigr)+\delta_{\beta}\bigl(y,(-1)^{\beta}(z-h_{\beta})\bigr)+(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{G}_{\beta}^{\prime}\bigl(J_{\beta}-\partial_{y_{1}}h_{\beta}\bigr)\\
&+\sum_{j=1}^{n}(\partial_{\nu}y_{j}-\delta_{1j})\left[\mathbb{G}_{\beta,j}-(-1)^{\beta}(\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}+\mathbb{G}_{\beta}^{\prime})\partial_{y_{j}}h_{\beta}\right].\end{split} $$

This provides the cancellation of the order $\varepsilon$ term $z\bar{\mathbb{H}}^{\prime}$ . We estimate the four displayed contributions separately. First,

$$ \|\partial_{\nu}y_{j}-\delta_{1j}\|_{C^{1,\theta}}\leq C\varepsilon(1+|z|^{3}),\qquad\|\widetilde{J}_{\beta}\|_{C^{1,\theta}}\leq C\varepsilon^{2}(1+|z|^{6}) $$

by the flow estimates and Lemma 4.17.

Moreover,

$$ \delta_{\beta}(y,z)=(1-\zeta_{\varepsilon}(z))w_{\beta}(y)z\bar{\mathbb{H}}^{\prime}(z) $$

is supported where $|z|\geq 4|\log\varepsilon|$ and has local $C^{1,\theta}$ norm at most $C\varepsilon^{2}e^{-|z|/2}$ . Finally, Corollary 5.10 bounds $\mathbb{G}_{\beta}^{\prime}$ and $\mathbb{G}_{\beta,j}$ by $C\varepsilon e^{-\sigma|z|}$ for any fixed $\sigma\in(1/2,1)$ . Absorbing the polynomial factors in $z$ into this exponential decay and applying the product inequality to (7.6) gives

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|N^{\beta}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{1}^{0,\beta}(y)\times(z-1,z+1))}\leq Ce^{-|z|/2}\bigl(&\varepsilon^{2}+\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{2}^{\beta}(y))}^{2}\\
&+\|\partial_{y_{1}}h_{\beta}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{2}^{0,\beta}(y))}\bigr).\end{split} $$

Apply (5.124) and (5.126) to the two norms of $h_{\beta}$ in (7.7). Their right-hand sides are bounded by $C\varepsilon^{2}$ , the squared ambient $C^{2,\theta}$ norm of $\phi$ , and the corresponding $A^{3/2}$ term, since the $A^{2}$ produced by squaring (5.124) is smaller than $A^{3/2}$ . Lastly,

$$ \sum_{\beta:\,|t_{\beta}|\leq 9|\log\varepsilon|}e^{-|t_{\beta}|/2}\leq C $$

by (6.19). Summing (7.7) in (7.4) proves (7.3). ∎

Fix $L>1$ , to be chosen large before $\varepsilon$ is chosen small, and retain the notation

$$ \begin{split}\Omega_{\alpha}^{1}&=\{|t_{\alpha}|<L\}\cap\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0},\\
\Omega_{\alpha}^{2}&=\{|t_{\alpha}|>L/2\}\cap\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0},\\
\Omega_{\alpha}^{3}&=\{|t_{\alpha}|\leq L/2\}\cap\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}.\end{split} $$

By separation, after $L$ is fixed we may assume that the strips $|t_{\alpha}|\leq 2L$ are contained in $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}$ on every neighbourhood used below.

#### 7.2. $C^{1,\theta}$ -estimates for $\phi$

#### Proposition 7.3 ( $C^{1,\theta}$ estimates).

There are constants $c,C>0$ independent of $L$ such that, for each sufficiently large fixed $L$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ depending on $L$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))}\leq{}&Ce^{-cL}\bigl(\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}\bigr)\\
&+C(L)\varepsilon^{2}+C(L)A(r+95|\log\varepsilon|;x).\end{split} $$

The proof will follow from combining Lemma 7.4 and Lemma 7.5 below.

#### 7.2.1. $C^{1,\theta}$ -outer estimates for $\phi$

#### Lemma 7.4.

For each fixed sufficiently large $L$ and sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\Omega_{\alpha}^{2})}\leq{}&Ce^{-cL}\bigl(\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+85|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}+\max_{\beta}\|H_{\beta}+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\beta}\cap B^{+}_{r+85|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}\bigr)\\
&+C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+85|\log\varepsilon|;x)+C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+85|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}.\end{split} $$

The constants in this estimate are independent of $L$ once $L$ is sufficiently large.

#### Proof.

We follow [29, Lemma 6.2 and (6.2)]. On $\{\min_{\beta}|t_{\beta}|>L/4\}$ set $U_{L}=W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*}+\mathbb{G}_{*})$ . The exponential estimates and (6.19) give $U_{L}\geq 1/2$ and $U_{L}+|\nabla U_{L}|\leq C$ , uniformly for large $L$ and small $\varepsilon$ . Equation (6.1) can therefore be written as

$$ \Delta\phi=U_{L}\phi+E_{\alpha}^{2}, $$

where we claim

$$ \displaystyle\|E_{\alpha}^{2}\|_{L^{\infty}(B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\{\min_{\beta}|t_{\beta}|>L/4\})} \displaystyle\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+80|\log\varepsilon|;x)+C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2} \displaystyle+Ce^{-cL}\max_{\beta}\|H_{\beta}+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\beta}\cap B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}. $$

Let us verify this estimate term by term at points $p\in B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\{\min_{\beta}|t_{\beta}|>L/4\}$ . In the bounds below, the norms of $h_{\beta}$ are on $B_{2}^{\beta}(\Pi_{\beta}(p))$ . The norms of $\phi$ and the quantity $A$ refer to $B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ and $A(r+80|\log\varepsilon|;x)$ , respectively; norms of $H_{\beta}+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}$ are on $\Sigma_{\beta}\cap B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ .

- • The difference

$$ W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*}+\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)-W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*}+\mathbb{G}_{*})-U_{L}\phi $$

is $O(\phi^{2})$ . The expression

$$ \mathcal{I}_{1}+\mathcal{I}_{2}+W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*}+\mathbb{G}_{*})-W^{\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\mathbb{G}_{*} $$

is bounded by Lemma 6.2, (6.14), and Corollary 5.10. These estimates give $C\varepsilon^{2}+CA+C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^{2}$ .

- • For every $\beta$ , Propositions 4.19 and 4.21 give $\displaystyle\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}={}$ $\displaystyle\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}(H_{\beta}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta})+O\bigl(e^{-|z|/2}(\varepsilon^{2}+\varepsilon\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{2,\theta}})\bigr),$ $\displaystyle|\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}|\leq{}$ $\displaystyle Ce^{-|z|/2}\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^{2}.$ Polynomial factors are absorbed by exponential decay. Summation using (6.19) gives $e^{-cL}$ in the outer region; (5.124), and Young’s inequality give the last line of (7.13) and the stated $C\varepsilon^{2}+CA+C\|\phi\|^{2}$ error.

- • Lemma 6.3 gives (7.14)

$$ \bigl\|-\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}-\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta}\bigr\|_{C^{\theta}}\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+C\varepsilon\max\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{2,\theta}}. $$

After (5.124) and Young’s inequality, the right-hand side of (7.14) is bounded by the first three terms on the right of (7.13).

This proves (7.13) uniformly in the number of sheets.

For $p\in B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\Omega_{\alpha}^{2}$ , every sheet distance exceeds $L/4$ on $B^{+}_{L/32}(p)$ , so we can apply Lemma F.4(i) iteratively on the concentric balls $B^{+}_{1+j\rho}(p)$ with Neumann condition on $\partial_{0}B^{+}_{1+j\rho}(p)$ . Choose $\rho>1$ , independently of $L$ , so that $C/\rho\leq 1/2$ in (F.15), and iterate for $\lfloor L/(64\rho)\rfloor$ steps. The remaining norm is $\|\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B^{+}_{1+\rho\lfloor L/(64\rho)\rfloor}(p))}$ , multiplied by at most $Ce^{-cL}$ . All these balls lie in $B^{+}_{L/32}(p)$ for sufficiently large $L$ . The contributions of $E_{\alpha}^{2}$ and $\partial_{\nu}\phi$ form a bounded geometric sum. Use (7.13) and Proposition 7.2 on these balls. The largest data ball is contained in $B^{+}_{r+1+L/64+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x)\subset B^{+}_{r+85|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ for fixed $L$ and small $\varepsilon$ . This estimates $\phi$ on every $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ ; restricting to $B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\Omega_{\alpha}^{2}$ proves (7.11). ∎

#### 7.2.2. $C^{1,\theta}$ -inner estimates for $\phi$

#### Lemma 7.5.

For each sufficiently large fixed $L$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\Omega_{\alpha}^{1})}\leq{}&Ce^{-cL}\bigl(\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}\\
&\quad+\max_{\beta}\|H_{\beta}+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\beta}\cap B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}\bigr)\\
&\quad+C(L)\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+95|\log\varepsilon|;x)+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}\bigr).\end{split} $$

We follow the cutoff–projection argument of [29, Section 6.2], and keep track the extra terms coming from the Neumann derivative at the boundary and the twisted coordinates. Fix $p\in B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\Omega_{\alpha}^{1}$ and put $y=\Pi_{\alpha}(p)$ . We estimate $\phi$ on $B_{1}^{+}(p)\cap\Omega_{\alpha}^{1}$ by estimating its pullback to the $\alpha$ -coordinates. The base of $Y_{\Sigma_{\alpha}}^{-1}(B_{1}^{+}(p))$ is contained in $B_{2}^{\alpha}(y)$ .

#### Claim 7.6 (Equation before projection).

In $\Omega^{1}_{\alpha}$

$$ (\Delta_{\alpha,0}+\partial_{zz}-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}))\phi=(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}(H_{\alpha}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha})+E_{\alpha}^{1}. $$

For $B_{r}^{+}(x)$ with $B^{+}_{r+30|\log\varepsilon|}(x)\subset B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|E_{\alpha}^{1}\|_{L^{\infty}(B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\{|t_{\alpha}|<2L\})}\leq C(L)\Bigl(&\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+30|\log\varepsilon|;x)+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+30|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}\Bigr).\end{split} $$

#### Proof.

We follow [29, Lemma 6.3] and estimate the additional correction and boundary terms. Using (6.35), the exact error in (7.16) is

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}E_{\alpha}^{1}={}&\mathcal{I}_{1}+\mathcal{I}_{2}+\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)+(W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}))\phi\\
&+(\Delta_{\alpha,0}-\Delta_{\alpha,z})\phi+H_{\alpha}(\cdot,z)\partial_{z}\phi-\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}\phi\\
&+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(H_{\alpha}(\cdot,z)-H_{\alpha}(\cdot,0)+(\Delta_{\alpha,z}-\Delta_{\alpha,0})h_{\alpha}\bigr)-\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}|\nabla_{\alpha,z}h_{\alpha}|^{2}\\
&+\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}\bigl((-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}-\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime\prime}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}\bigr)-\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}-\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta}.\end{split} $$

For fixed $L$ , separation places $B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\{|t_{\alpha}|<2L\}$ in $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}$ once $\varepsilon$ is small. To obtain the pointwise estimates below, take $p\in B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\{|t_{\alpha}|<2L\}$ . Norms of $\phi$ are taken on $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ , and norms of $h_{\beta}$ on $B_{2}^{\beta}(\Pi_{\beta}(p))$ ; their bounds are then replaced by those on $B^{+}_{r+30|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ and its sheet intersections. In these bounds $A$ means $A(r+30|\log\varepsilon|;x)$ .

- • The sum

$$ \mathcal{I}_{1}+\mathcal{I}_{2}+\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)+(W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}))\phi $$

is bounded by $C(L)(\varepsilon^{2}+A+\|\phi\|_{C^{0}}^{2})$ , by Lemma 6.2, (6.14), and $|\mathbb{H}_{*}-\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}|\leq C(L)e^{-D_{\alpha}}$ .

- • The terms

$$ (\Delta_{\alpha,0}-\Delta_{\alpha,z})\phi+H_{\alpha}(\cdot,z)\partial_{z}\phi-\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}\phi $$

and

$$ (-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}\bigl(H_{\alpha}(\cdot,z)-H_{\alpha}(\cdot,0)+(\Delta_{\alpha,z}-\Delta_{\alpha,0})h_{\alpha}\bigr)-\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\alpha}|\nabla_{\alpha,z}h_{\alpha}|^{2} $$

are bounded by

$$ C(L)\bigl(\varepsilon\|\phi\|_{C^{2}}+\varepsilon^{2}+\varepsilon\|h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{2}}+\|h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{1}}^{2}\bigr). $$

Use Propositions 4.19 and 4.21, (6.5), then (5.124) and Young’s inequality.

- • The sum

$$ \sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}\bigl((-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}-\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}\bigr) $$

is bounded by $C(L)A$ : its coefficients are uniformly bounded and the exponentially decaying factors sum to at most $C(L)e^{-D_{\alpha}}$ . Finally,

$$ -\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}-\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta} $$

is controlled by Lemma 6.3 and (7.14), followed by (5.124) and Young’s inequality.

#### 7.2.3. Cut-off and project

Choose $\tilde{\xi}\in C_{c}^{\infty}((-2L,2L))$ with $0\leq\tilde{\xi}\leq 1$ , $\tilde{\xi}=1$ on $[-L,L]$ , and $|\tilde{\xi}^{\prime}|\leq C_{*}/L$ , $|\tilde{\xi}^{\prime\prime}|\leq C_{*}/L^{2}$ . Define

$$ \phi_{\alpha}(y,z)=\tilde{\xi}(z)\phi(y,z)-c_{\alpha}(y)\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}(y,z), $$

where

$$ c_{\alpha}(y)=\frac{\int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi(y,z)(\tilde{\xi}(z)-1)\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}(y,z)\,dz}{\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}(y,z))^{2}\,dz}, $$

so that

$$ \int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi_{\alpha}(y,z)\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}(y,z)\,dz=0. $$

#### Claim 7.7 (Estimates for the projection coefficient).

For any $y\in\Sigma_{\alpha}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle|c_{\alpha}(y)| \displaystyle\leq Ce^{-L}\sup_{L<|z|<9|\log\varepsilon|}|\phi(y,z)|, \displaystyle|\nabla_{\alpha,0}c_{\alpha}(y)| \displaystyle\leq Ce^{-L}\sup_{L<|z|<9|\log\varepsilon|}\bigl(|\phi(y,z)|+|\nabla_{\alpha,0}\phi(y,z)|\bigr), \displaystyle\|c_{\alpha}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{1}^{\alpha}(y))} \displaystyle\leq Ce^{-L}\|\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{2}^{\alpha}(y)\times[-9|\log\varepsilon|,9|\log\varepsilon|])}. $$

For $y\in\partial_{0}\Sigma_{\alpha}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}(\partial_{y_{1}}c_{\alpha})\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime})^{2}\,dz={}&\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\partial_{y_{1}}\phi)(\tilde{\xi}-1)\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\,dz\\
&-(-1)^{\alpha}(\partial_{y_{1}}h_{\alpha})\int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi(\tilde{\xi}-1)\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}\,dz.\end{split} $$

In particular,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|\partial_{y_{1}}c_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{1}^{0,\alpha}(y))}\leq Ce^{-L}\bigl(&\|\partial_{y_{1}}\phi\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{2}^{0,\alpha}(y)\times[-9|\log\varepsilon|,9|\log\varepsilon|])}\\
&+\|\partial_{y_{1}}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{2}^{0,\alpha}(y))}\|\phi\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{2}^{0,\alpha}(y)\times[-9|\log\varepsilon|,9|\log\varepsilon|])}\bigr).\end{split} $$

#### Proof.

The factor $\tilde{\xi}-1$ vanishes for $|z|\leq L$ , while $|\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}|+|\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}|+|\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime\prime}|\leq Ce^{-|z|}$ . Integrating this bound gives (7.22). For any $i=1,\ldots,n$ , differentiation of (7.20) under the integral gives

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}(\partial_{y_{i}}c_{\alpha})\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime})^{2}\,dz={}&\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\partial_{y_{i}}\phi)(\tilde{\xi}-1)\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\,dz\\
&-(-1)^{\alpha}(\partial_{y_{i}}h_{\alpha})\int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi(\tilde{\xi}-1)\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}\,dz.\end{split} $$

This proves (7.23) and (7.25). Now subtract (7.27) at two points $y,\bar{y}$ and use the Hölder product inequality. The differences of the correction factors are bounded by $Ce^{-|z|}|h_{\alpha}(y)-h_{\alpha}(\bar{y})|$ , and the differences of the other factors are estimated by their $C^{\theta}$ seminorms. Integration over $|z|>L$ , using the bounded $C^{2,\theta}$ norm of $h_{\alpha}$ , proves (7.24) and (7.26). ∎

#### Claim 7.8 (Equation after projection).

For base points $y\in\Sigma_{\alpha}$ on which $c_{\alpha}$ is defined as above, and for every $z\in\mathbb{R}$ ,

$$ (\Delta_{\alpha,0}+\partial_{zz}-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}))\phi_{\alpha}=p_{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}+F_{\alpha}, $$

where

and

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|\partial_{y_{1}}\phi_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}}\leq{}&Ce^{-L}\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}\\
&+C(L)\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+95|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/2}+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^{2}\bigr).\end{split} $$

We also note that by the definition of $\phi_{\alpha}$ in (7.19) $\phi_{\alpha}$ has uniform exponential decay in $z$ for all $y$ . By choosing $L$ sufficiently large, we can conclude the proof by arguing as in [29, page 26, (6.6)] using the inner gluing estimates for the linearized operator in Appendix F. Indeed, the equation in Claim 7.8 and the orthogonality (7.21) allow us to use Proposition F.3.

Fix $\rho>1$ , independently of $L$ , so that $C/\rho\leq 1/2$ and repeat the fixed-step iteration used in Lemma 7.4, starting at radius 2. After $\lfloor L/(64\rho)\rfloor$ steps, the norm $\|\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}}$ has coefficient $2^{-\lfloor L/(64\rho)\rfloor}\leq Ce^{-cL}$ , while the $F_{\alpha}$ and boundary terms on the right-hand side only have a bounded factor coming from summing a geometric series. By (7.19) and (7.24),

$$ \|\phi_{\alpha}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{2+k\rho}^{\alpha}(y)\times\mathbb{R})}\leq C\|\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}. $$

Substituting (7.34)-(7.35) and using $A^{3/2}\leq A$ gives the required estimate for $\phi_{\alpha}$ on $B_{2}^{\alpha}(y)\times\mathbb{R}$ . On $Y_{\Sigma_{\alpha}}^{-1}(B_{1}^{+}(p)\cap\Omega_{\alpha}^{1})$ we have $|z|<L$ , hence $\phi=\phi_{\alpha}+c_{\alpha}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\alpha}$ . Equation (7.24) bounds the added term there by $Ce^{-L}\|\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}$ . Taking the supremum over $p\in B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\Omega_{\alpha}^{1}$ proves (7.15) ∎

#### Proof of Proposition 7.3.

Notice that the inner and outer regions overlap and cover the domain. Use (7.11) and (7.15) after enlarging all domains in the right-hand side to $B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ . Their sum gives (7.10) with the additional term $C(L)\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}$ . After fixing $L$ , choose $\varepsilon$ so small that this term is at most $e^{-cL}\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+95|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}$ . This proves (7.10). ∎

#### 7.3. $C^{2,\theta}$ -estimates for $\phi$

Let us begin by recording the following estimate which will be needed later to apply Schauder theory.

#### Claim 7.9.

For each ball $B_{r}^{+}(x)$ with $B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x)\subset B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|\Delta\phi-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))}\lesssim\;&\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+80|\log\varepsilon|;x)+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}\\
&+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}.\end{split} $$

#### Proof.

We follow [29, Appendix C, (2)–(6)] for the terms already present in the ordinary Fermi-coordinate calculation, and estimate the boundary-correction and twisted-coordinate contributions separately.

By (6.35), we have

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\Delta\phi-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi={}&\mathcal{I}_{1}+\mathcal{I}_{2}+\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)+\sum_{\beta}\bigl((-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}-\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime\prime}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}\bigr)\\
&-\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}-\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta}.\end{split} $$

Split $\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}$ into

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}(y,z)={} \displaystyle H_{\beta}(y,0)+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}(y) \displaystyle+[H_{\beta}(y,z)-H_{\beta}(y,0)]+(\Delta_{\beta,z}-\Delta_{\beta,0})h_{\beta}(y). $$

The estimates in [29, Appendix C, (2)–(6)] apply to $\mathcal{I}_{1}$ and the sums in $\beta$ of

$$ \mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}[H_{\beta}(y,z)-H_{\beta}(y,0)],\qquad\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}(\Delta_{\beta,z}-\Delta_{\beta,0})h_{\beta},\qquad\mathbb{H}^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}|\nabla_{\beta,z}h_{\beta}|^{2}, $$

using here Lemma 6.2, Propositions 4.19 and 4.21, and (5.124). Their $C^{\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))$ norms are bounded by

$$ C\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+80|\log\varepsilon|;x)+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}\bigr). $$

For $H_{\beta}(y,z)-H_{\beta}(y,0)$ , Proposition 4.19 controls the tangential derivatives; the Riccati equation and $\partial_{z}=\widetilde{Z}_{\beta}+T$ control its normal derivative. Multiplication by $\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}$ absorbs the polynomial factors in $z$ . All sums are controlled uniformly by (6.19).

For $p\in B_{r}^{+}(x)$ and each index with $|t_{\beta}(p)|<9|\log\varepsilon|$ , put $(y,z)=(\Pi_{\beta}(p),t_{\beta}(p))$ . For the first line of (7.38), use

$$ \|\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}(H_{\beta}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta})\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(y,z))}\leq Ce^{-|z|/2}\|H_{\beta}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{2}^{\beta}(y))}. $$

Apply (6.44), including both terms on its last line, to the norm on the right, and sum using (6.19). This bounds

$$ \Bigl\|\sum_{\beta}(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}^{\prime}_{\beta}(H_{\beta}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta})\Bigr\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))} $$

by the right-hand side of (7.36). Here $\Pi_{\beta}(p)$ is joined to $p$ by a twisted flow segment with time length less than $9|\log\varepsilon|$ . The sheet ball $B_{2}^{\beta}(\Pi_{\beta}(p))$ and the balls required when applying (6.44) on that set, with its additional $25|\log\varepsilon|$ radius, lie in $B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ .

Finally, (6.14), Lemma 6.2, Corollary 5.10, and (7.14), combined with (5.124) and Young’s inequality, give

$$ \displaystyle\Bigl\|\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)+\mathcal{I}_{2}-\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}-\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta}\Bigr\|_{C^{\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))} \displaystyle\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+80|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/2}+C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+80|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}. $$

Combining these bounds in (7.37), using $A^{3/2}\leq A$ , proves (7.36). ∎

#### Lemma 7.10 ( $C^{2,\theta}$ estimates).

For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ , the estimate (7.1) holds. Equivalently, for $x\in B^{+}_{6R/7}(0)$ and $0<r<R/60$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))}+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}+\max_{\alpha}\|h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{2,\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\\
&\hskip 99.58464pt\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+100|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x).\end{split} $$

#### Proof.

The argument follows the proof of [29, Section 6.3, especially (6.8)]. For each $p\in B_{r}^{+}(x)$ , apply the interior or Neumann Schauder estimate in Proposition E.1 on $B_{2}^{+}(p)$ , with data on $\partial_{0}B_{2}^{+}(p)$ when that set is nonempty, to estimate $\phi$ on $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ . Since $B_{2}^{+}(p)\subset B^{+}_{r+2}(x)$ , taking the supremum over $p$ gives

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))}\leq C\bigl(&\|\phi\|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r+2}(x))}+\|\Delta\phi-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi\|_{C^{\theta}(B^{+}_{r+2}(x))}\\
&+\|\partial_{\nu}\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(\partial_{0}B^{+}_{r+2}(x))}\bigr).\end{split} $$

The coefficient $W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})$ has a uniform $C^{\theta}(B_{2}^{+}(p))$ bound for these centres $p$ .

Fix $L$ so large that the coefficient $Ce^{-cL}$ in (7.10), after multiplication by the Schauder constant, is less than $1/128$ . The qualitative convergence supplied by Lemmas 4.31-4.32, Proposition 5.7, and Corollary 5.10 implies that, after decreasing $\varepsilon$ with this $L$ fixed,

$$ C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}+C\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}\leq\frac{1}{128}. $$

Now apply (7.10) to $\|\phi\|_{C^{0}}$ in (7.40), Claim 7.9 to $\Delta\phi-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi$ , and Proposition 7.2 to $\partial_{\nu}\phi$ . Then enlarge the right-hand domains to $B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ . We have

$$ C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{128}\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}},\quad C\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{128}\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}}, $$

with the norms of $\phi$ on $B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ and the norms of $H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}$ on $\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ . Since $A^{3/2}\leq A$ , we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))}\leq{}&\frac{1}{32}\Bigl(\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}\\
&\qquad+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}\Bigr)\\
&+C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+100|\log\varepsilon|;x).\end{split} $$

Next apply (6.44) and consider

$$ C\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}}^{2}\quad\text{and}\quad C\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^{2} $$

where the norms are taken, respectively, on $\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ and $B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ . By (7.41), followed by adding the resulting estimate to (7.42), we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x))}+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\\
&\quad\leq\frac{1}{16}\Bigl(\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+100|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}\Bigr)\\
&\qquad+C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+100|\log\varepsilon|;x).\end{split} $$

This is the analogue of [29, (6.8)].

Iterate (7.43) $k=\lceil 3|\log\varepsilon|/4\rceil$ times, increasing the radius by $100|\log\varepsilon|$ at each step. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ ,

$$ 16^{-k}\leq\varepsilon^{2},\qquad 2+100k|\log\varepsilon|\leq 50|\log\varepsilon|^{2}. $$

Start the iteration at radius $r+2$ . After $k$ steps, the remaining norms are $\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+2+100k|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}$ and $\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+2+100k|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}$ , both uniformly bounded, while $A$ is nondecreasing in its radius and $\sum_{j\geq 0}16^{-j}=16/15$ . Hence

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{r+2}^{+}(x))}+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r+2}^{+}(x))}\\
&\hskip 85.35826pt\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+100|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x).\end{split} $$

The intermediate balls $B^{+}_{r+2+100j|\log\varepsilon|}(x)$ , $0\leq j\leq k$ , remain in $B^{+}_{7R/8-2}(0)$ by the fixed outer margin. Finally, apply (5.124) on $B_{1}^{\alpha}(y)$ for each $y\in\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x)$ . Equation (7.44), followed by the supremum over $y$ , gives the $C^{2,\theta}$ bound for $h_{\alpha}$ and proves (7.39). ∎

#### Corollary 7.11 (Toda system with the first error improvement).

For $x\in B^{+}_{6R/7}(0)$ and $0<r<R/60$ , the Toda system is

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}H_{\alpha}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}(y)={}&\frac{2}{\sigma_{0}}\left(A_{(-1)^{\alpha-1}}^{2}e^{-|t_{\alpha-1}(y,0)|}-A_{(-1)^{\alpha}}^{2}e^{-|t_{\alpha+1}(y,0)|}\right)+E_{\alpha}^{0}(y),\end{split} $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\max_{\alpha}\|E_{\alpha}^{0}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\lesssim\;&\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2}+\varepsilon^{1/3}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x).\end{split} $$

#### Proof.

Equation (7.45) is the rough Toda equation (6.36). It remains to improve the estimate for $E_{\alpha}^{0}$ . From (6.37),

$$ \displaystyle\max_{\alpha}\|E_{\alpha}^{0}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\leq C\bigl( \displaystyle\varepsilon^{2}+\varepsilon^{1/3}A(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)+A(r+25|\log\varepsilon|;x)^{3/2} \displaystyle+\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2} \displaystyle+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}\bigr). $$

Apply Lemma 7.10 with centre radius $r+25|\log\varepsilon|$ . The sum of the two displayed squared norms is estimated on a ball contained in the one below, since

$$ r+25|\log\varepsilon|+100|\log\varepsilon|^{2}\leq r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2} $$

for small $\varepsilon$ . Lemma 7.10 then gives

$$ \displaystyle\max_{\alpha}\|H_{\alpha}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2}+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+25|\log\varepsilon|}(x))}^{2} \displaystyle\qquad\leq C\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)\bigr)^{2}\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2}. $$

Monotonicity of $A$ in the radius now gives (7.46). ∎

For the differentiated form of the Toda system, restrict to the already defined logarithmic strip by setting

$$ \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\alpha}^{0}=\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}\cap\{|t_{\alpha}|<10|\log\varepsilon|\}. $$

This does not change the definition of $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}$ . As usual, write $h_{\alpha,i}=\partial_{y_{i}}h_{\alpha}$ and $H_{\alpha,i}(y,0)=\partial_{y_{i}}H_{\alpha}(y,0)$ .

#### Corollary 7.12 (Differentiated Toda system).

For $i=1,\ldots,n$ , in $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\alpha}^{0}$ one has

$$ \mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(H_{\alpha,i}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}(y)\bigr)=\partial_{y_{i}}\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,1,i}+\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,2,i}, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&\|\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,1,i}\|_{C^{\theta}(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\alpha}^{0}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}+\|\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,2,i}\|_{C^{0}(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\alpha}^{0}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\\
&\qquad\leq C\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2}+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)\bigr).\end{split} $$

#### Proof.

The graphical ordering gives $t_{\alpha-1}(y,0)>0$ and $t_{\alpha+1}(y,0)<0$ . Differentiating (7.45) in $y_{i}$ gives

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}H_{\alpha,i}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}={}&-\frac{2}{\sigma_{0}}\Bigl[A_{(-1)^{\alpha-1}}^{2}(\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\alpha-1})e^{-t_{\alpha-1}}+A_{(-1)^{\alpha}}^{2}(\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\alpha+1})e^{t_{\alpha+1}}\Bigr]\\
&+\partial_{y_{i}}E_{\alpha}^{0}+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}-\partial_{y_{i}}\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}.\end{split} $$

Set

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,1,i}={} \displaystyle\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}E_{\alpha}^{0}, \displaystyle\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,2,i}={} \displaystyle-\frac{2}{\sigma_{0}}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\Bigl[A_{(-1)^{\alpha-1}}^{2}(\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\alpha-1})e^{-t_{\alpha-1}}+A_{(-1)^{\alpha}}^{2}(\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\alpha+1})e^{t_{\alpha+1}}\Bigr] \displaystyle+\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}-\partial_{y_{i}}\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\bigr)+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}h_{\alpha,i}E_{\alpha}^{0}. $$

Since $\partial_{y_{i}}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}=-(-1)^{\alpha}h_{\alpha,i}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}$ , the product rule in $\partial_{y_{i}}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}E_{\alpha}^{0})$ and (7.49) prove (7.47).

In the estimates that follow, ambient norms are on $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\alpha}^{0}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x)$ and sheet norms on $\Pi_{\alpha}(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\alpha}^{0}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))$ . We estimate separately the exponential-distance expression in the first line of $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,2,i}$ , the commutator $\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}-\partial_{y_{i}}\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}$ , and the factors $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}E_{\alpha}^{0}$ and $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}h_{\alpha,i}E_{\alpha}^{0}$ .

- • If $|t_{\alpha\pm 1}(y,0)|\leq 10|\log\varepsilon|$ , Proposition 4.26 gives $|\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\alpha\pm 1}(y,0)|\leq C\varepsilon^{1/6}$ . If $|t_{\alpha\pm 1}(y,0)|>10|\log\varepsilon|$ , then $e^{-|t_{\alpha\pm 1}(y,0)|}\leq\varepsilon^{10}$ and $|\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\alpha\pm 1}|\leq C$ . Hence (7.51)

$$ \sum_{\beta=\alpha-1,\alpha+1}|\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\beta}|e^{-|t_{\beta}|}\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+C\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x). $$

- • By the commutator estimate (4.71),

$$ |\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}-\partial_{y_{i}}\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}|\leq C\varepsilon\bigl(|\nabla_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}|+|\nabla_{\alpha,0}^{2}h_{\alpha}|\bigr). $$

Lemma 7.10 therefore gives (7.52)

$$ |\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}-\partial_{y_{i}}\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}|\leq C\varepsilon^{3}+C\varepsilon A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+C\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x). $$

- • Corollary 7.11 and the bounded $C^{\theta}$ norms of $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}$ and $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}$ give

$$ \|\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}E_{\alpha}^{0}\|_{C^{\theta}}\leq C\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+A^{3/2}+\varepsilon^{1/3}A\bigr), $$

where $A=A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)$ . Moreover, Proposition 5.7 gives $\|h_{\alpha,i}\|_{C^{0}}=o(1)$ uniformly, so

$$ \|(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}h_{\alpha,i}E_{\alpha}^{0}\|_{C^{0}}\leq C\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+A^{3/2}+\varepsilon^{1/3}A\bigr). $$

Combining (7.51), (7.52), and the two displayed estimates for $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}E_{\alpha}^{0}$ and $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}h_{\alpha,i}E_{\alpha}^{0}$ , and using $\varepsilon^{1/3}\leq\varepsilon^{1/6}$ , proves (7.48). ∎

### 8. Improved horizontal estimates for $\phi_{y_{i}}$ and improved Toda system

We improve the $C^{1,\theta}$ estimates for the horizontal derivatives of the error. Throughout this section, $\phi_{y_{i}}=\partial_{y_{i}}\phi$ , $1\leq i\leq n$ , in the twisted Fermi coordinates with respect to the sheet under consideration. The argument follows the inner–outer decomposition of [29, Section 7], with the addition of the boundary terms and the twisted-coordinate errors.

Let $K\geq 10$ be fixed. The constants may depend on $K$ and $\theta$ , but not on the number of sheets. By decreasing $\varepsilon_{0}$ , the same estimates hold on every fixed larger logarithmic strip.

#### Proposition 8.1 (Improved horizontal derivative estimates).

For $x\in B^{+}_{5R/6}(0)$ , $0<r<R/70$ , and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\max_{\begin{subarray}{c}\alpha\\
1\leq i\leq n\end{subarray}}\|\phi_{y_{i}}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}\cap\{|t_{\alpha}|\leq K|\log\varepsilon|\})}\lesssim\; \displaystyle\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+200|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2} \displaystyle+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+200|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x). $$

In particular, (8.1) controls every second derivative of $\phi$ containing at least one horizontal derivative.

#### Corollary 8.2 (Horizontal derivatives of the shifts).

Under the hypotheses of Proposition 8.1,

$$ \displaystyle\max_{\alpha}\|\nabla_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\lesssim\; \displaystyle\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+200|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2} \displaystyle+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+200|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x). $$

#### Corollary 8.3 (Toda system with improved error).

Under the same hypotheses,

$$ \displaystyle H_{\alpha}(y,0)={} \displaystyle\frac{2}{\sigma_{0}}\Bigl(A_{(-1)^{\alpha-1}}^{2}e^{-|t_{\alpha-1}(y,0)|}-A_{(-1)^{\alpha}}^{2}e^{-|t_{\alpha+1}(y,0)|}\Bigr) \displaystyle+E_{\alpha}^{0}(y)-\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}(y), $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\max_{\alpha}\|E_{\alpha}^{0}-\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\Sigma_{\alpha}\cap B_{r}^{+}(x))}\lesssim\; \displaystyle\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+200|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2} \displaystyle+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+200|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x). $$

The proofs are completed after we obtain the inner estimate Lemma 8.8. Until then, let $x\in B^{+}_{5R/6}(0)$ and $0<r<R/65$ ; the smaller range $r<R/70$ in the conclusions leaves room for iteration.

#### 8.1. Boundary estimates and the equation for $\phi_{y_{i}}$

#### Proposition 8.4 (Boundary data for horizontal derivatives).

For every $p\in\partial_{0}B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}\cap\{|t_{\alpha}|\leq K|\log\varepsilon|\}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\|\partial_{\nu}\phi_{y_{i}}\|_{C^{\theta}(\partial_{0}B_{1}^{+}(p))}+\|\partial_{y_{1}}\phi_{y_{i}}\|_{C^{\theta}(\partial_{0}B_{1}^{+}(p))}\lesssim\; \displaystyle\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2} \displaystyle+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x),\qquad 2\leq i\leq n, $$

and

$$ \displaystyle\|\phi_{y_{1}}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(\partial_{0}B_{1}^{+}(p))}\lesssim\; \displaystyle\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2} \displaystyle+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x). $$

These are boundary norms: derivatives are taken only in the variables tangent to the boundary. If $n=1$ , only (8.6) is needed.

#### Proof.

Proposition 7.2 and Proposition 7.1, applied on the enlarged balls occurring in (7.3), give

$$ \|\partial_{\nu}\phi\|_{C^{1,\theta}(\partial_{0}B_{r+2}^{+}(x))}\leq C\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2}\bigr). $$

Indeed, since $0<A\leq 1$ by definition, the square in (7.3) is bounded by $C(\varepsilon^{2}+A)^{2}\leq C(\varepsilon^{2}+A^{3/2})$ , with $A$ evaluated at the radius in (8.7). On the boundary, the differentiated flow estimates and (4.73)-(4.75) yield

$$ \|\partial_{y_{1}}-\partial_{\nu}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(\partial_{0}B_{1}^{+}(p))}+\sum_{j=2}^{n}\|[\partial_{\nu},\partial_{y_{j}}]\|_{C^{\theta}(\partial_{0}B_{1}^{+}(p))}+\|[\partial_{\nu},\partial_{z}]\|_{C^{\theta}(\partial_{0}B_{1}^{+}(p))}\leq C\varepsilon(1+|z|^{2}). $$

Here a norm of a vector field means the corresponding norm of its coefficients. At $z=0$ , the coefficients of $\partial_{y_{1}}-\partial_{\nu}$ vanish. Their $C^{0}$ bound follows by integrating in $z$ ; the first and second derivatives of all coefficients in (8.8) follow from Lemmas 4.10 and 4.12, together with the rescaled metric bounds. The mean value theorem gives the stated Hölder seminorms.

For later use, on $|z|\leq K|\log\varepsilon|+2$ ,

$$ \varepsilon^{3}(1+|\log\varepsilon|^{6})\leq C\varepsilon^{2},\qquad\varepsilon(1+|\log\varepsilon|^{6})\leq C\varepsilon^{1/6}. $$

If $i\geq 2$ , then $\partial_{y_{i}}$ is tangent to the boundary and

$$ \partial_{\nu}\phi_{y_{i}}=\partial_{y_{i}}(\partial_{\nu}\phi)+[\partial_{\nu},\partial_{y_{i}}]\phi. $$

The first term is bounded by (8.7); the second is bounded by (8.8), Proposition 7.1, and (8.9). This proves the estimate for $\partial_{\nu}\phi_{y_{i}}$ in (8.5). Since

$$ \partial_{y_{1}}\phi_{y_{i}}=\partial_{\nu}\phi_{y_{i}}+(\partial_{y_{1}}-\partial_{\nu})\phi_{y_{i}}, $$

the same estimates prove the second term in (8.5).

For $i=1$ we do not differentiate the Neumann condition in the transverse direction. Instead, on the boundary,

$$ \phi_{y_{1}}=\partial_{\nu}\phi+(\partial_{y_{1}}-\partial_{\nu})\phi. $$

For $2\leq j\leq n$ ,

$$ \partial_{y_{j}}\bigl((\partial_{y_{1}}-\partial_{\nu})\phi\bigr)=(\partial_{y_{1}}-\partial_{\nu})\phi_{y_{j}}+[\partial_{\nu},\partial_{y_{j}}]\phi, $$

and

$$ \partial_{z}\bigl((\partial_{y_{1}}-\partial_{\nu})\phi\bigr)=(\partial_{y_{1}}-\partial_{\nu})\partial_{z}\phi+[\partial_{\nu},\partial_{z}]\phi. $$

Thus (8.7)-(8.9) control the full boundary $C^{1,\theta}$ norm of the right-hand side of (8.10), proving (8.6). ∎

We next isolate the derivative of a $C^{\theta}$ remainder, as in the interior calculation of [29, Lemma 7.2].

#### Lemma 8.5 (Equation for the horizontal derivatives).

Write $H_{\alpha,i}(y,0)=\partial_{y_{i}}H_{\alpha}(y,0)$ and $h_{\alpha,i}=\partial_{y_{i}}h_{\alpha}$ . Set

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}={} \displaystyle\widetilde{E}_{0,\alpha}+\widetilde{E}_{e,\alpha}, \displaystyle\widetilde{E}_{0,\alpha}={} \displaystyle H_{\alpha}(y,z)\partial_{z}\phi+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(H_{\alpha}(y,z)-H_{\alpha}(y,0)+(\Delta_{\alpha,z}-\Delta_{\alpha,0})h_{\alpha}\bigr) \displaystyle-\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}|\nabla_{\alpha,z}h_{\alpha}|^{2}+\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}\bigl((-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}-\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime\prime}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}\bigr)-\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}, $$

where, in the sum over $\beta\neq\alpha$ , $\mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}$ and $\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}$ are those in (6.2), and

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{E}_{e,\alpha}={} \displaystyle(\Delta_{\alpha,0}-\Delta_{\alpha,z})\phi-\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}\phi+\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)+\mathcal{I}_{2}-\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}+\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta}. $$

Then

$$ (\Delta_{\alpha,0}+\partial_{zz})\phi=W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(H_{\alpha}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\bigr)+\mathcal{I}_{1}+\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}, $$

and, in the distributional sense,

$$ (\Delta_{\alpha,0}+\partial_{zz}-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}))\phi_{y_{i}}=(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(H_{\alpha,i}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}\bigr)+\partial_{y_{i}}\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}+E^{i}+\partial_{y_{i}}\mathcal{I}_{1}, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle E^{i}={} \displaystyle[\Delta_{\alpha,0},\partial_{y_{i}}]\phi+\bigl(W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha})\bigr)\phi_{y_{i}} \displaystyle+W^{\prime\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi\sum_{\beta}(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}\Bigl(\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\beta}-\sum_{j=1}^{n}(h_{\beta,j}\circ\Pi_{\beta})\partial_{y_{i}}\Pi_{\beta}^{j}\Bigr) \displaystyle+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(\partial_{y_{i}}\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}-\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}\bigr)-\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}h_{\alpha,i}\bigl(H_{\alpha}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\bigr). $$

The sum in the second line of (8.15) includes $\beta=\alpha$ .

#### Proof.

Move the mean-curvature term and the difference $\Delta_{\alpha,z}-\Delta_{\alpha,0}$ in (6.1) to the right, and use (6.10). The coefficient of $(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}$ at height zero is $H_{\alpha}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}$ ; the remaining terms are exactly (8.11) and (8.12). This proves (8.13).

Differentiating (8.13) gives

$$ \partial_{y_{i}}\bigl(W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi\bigr)=W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi_{y_{i}}+W^{\prime\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi\,\partial_{y_{i}}\mathbb{H}_{*}, $$

with

$$ \partial_{y_{i}}\mathbb{H}_{*}=\sum_{\beta}(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}\Bigl(\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\beta}-\sum_{j=1}^{n}(h_{\beta,j}\circ\Pi_{\beta})\partial_{y_{i}}\Pi_{\beta}^{j}\Bigr). $$

Moreover,

$$ \displaystyle\partial_{y_{i}}\Bigl[(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(H_{\alpha}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\bigr)\Bigr]={} \displaystyle(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(H_{\alpha,i}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}\bigr) \displaystyle+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(\partial_{y_{i}}\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}-\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}\bigr) \displaystyle-\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}h_{\alpha,i}\bigl(H_{\alpha}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}\bigr). $$

Here $\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\alpha}=0$ , $\partial_{y_{i}}\Pi_{\alpha}^{j}=\delta_{i}^{j}$ , and $\partial_{y_{i}}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}=-(-1)^{\alpha}h_{\alpha,i}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}$ . Commuting $\partial_{y_{i}}$ past $\Delta_{\alpha,0}$ and subtracting $W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha})\phi_{y_{i}}$ proves (8.14)-(8.15). ∎

#### Lemma 8.6 (Bounds for the differentiated equation).

On $B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}\cap\{|t_{\alpha}|\leq K|\log\varepsilon|\}$ ,

$$ \|\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}\|_{C^{\theta}(\mathcal{M}^{0}_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r}(x))}\lesssim\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2}, $$

$$ \displaystyle\|E^{i}\|_{C^{0}(\mathcal{M}^{0}_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r}(x))}\lesssim\; \displaystyle\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2}+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x), $$

and

$$ \displaystyle\|\partial_{y_{i}}\mathcal{I}_{1}\|_{C^{0}(\mathcal{M}^{0}_{\alpha}\cap B^{+}_{r}(x))}\lesssim\; \displaystyle\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{2}+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x). $$

The same estimates hold on every fixed enlargement $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{\lambda}$ , with constants also depending on $\lambda$ .

Fix $p\in B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}\cap\{|t_{\alpha}|\leq K|\log\varepsilon|\}$ . We estimate the expressions below on $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ . Notice that Proposition 7.1 gives bounds for $\phi$ , $h_{\beta}$ , and $H_{\beta}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}$ , respectively in $C^{2,\theta}$ , $C^{2,\theta}$ , and $C^{\theta}$ , by

$$ C\varepsilon^{2}+CA(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x). $$

For the first three linear expressions in (8.11)-(8.12),

$$ H_{\alpha}(y,z)\partial_{z}\phi,\qquad(\Delta_{\alpha,0}-\Delta_{\alpha,z})\phi,\qquad-\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}\phi, $$

Proposition 4.19 and (6.5) give the bound $C\varepsilon(1+|z|^{2})\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}$ . Substitution of (8.19) uses

$$ \varepsilon(1+|\log\varepsilon|^{2})A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)\leq\frac{2}{3}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2}+\frac{1}{3}\varepsilon^{3}(1+|\log\varepsilon|^{2})^{3}, $$

whose last term is $O(\varepsilon^{2})$ .

The two expressions

$$ (-1)^{\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}\bigl(H_{\alpha}(y,z)-H_{\alpha}(y,0)+(\Delta_{\alpha,z}-\Delta_{\alpha,0})h_{\alpha}\bigr),\qquad-\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}|\nabla_{\alpha,z}h_{\alpha}|^{2}, $$

have local $C^{\theta}$ norm at most $C\varepsilon^{2}+C\varepsilon\|h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{2,\theta}}+C\|h_{\alpha}\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^{2}$ ; the polynomial factors in $z$ are absorbed by the exponential decay of $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}$ and $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}$ .

For $\beta\neq\alpha$ , write in the $\beta$ -coordinates

$$ \mathcal{R}_{\beta,1}=H_{\beta}(y,0)+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}+H_{\beta}(y,z)-H_{\beta}(y,0)+(\Delta_{\beta,z}-\Delta_{\beta,0})h_{\beta}. $$

On $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}$ , separation and the closest-sheet property give

$$ \sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}\bigl(\|\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}\|_{C^{\theta}}+\|\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime\prime}\|_{C^{\theta}}\bigr)\leq CA(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{1/2}+C\varepsilon^{2}. $$

The contribution

$$ \sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}\bigl(H_{\beta}(\cdot,0)+\Delta_{\beta,0}h_{\beta}\bigr) $$

is bounded by the product of (8.19) and the sum above. The terms containing $H_{\beta}(y,z)-H_{\beta}(y,0)$ , $(\Delta_{\beta,z}-\Delta_{\beta,0})h_{\beta}$ , and $\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime\prime}\mathcal{R}_{\beta,2}$ are estimated as for the two $\alpha$ -sheet expressions above. Their sum is $C(\varepsilon^{2}+A^{3/2})$ at the radius in (8.16).

Finally,

$$ \|\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{G}_{*}+\phi)\|_{C^{\theta}}\leq C(\varepsilon+\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}})^{2},\quad\|\mathcal{I}_{2}\|_{C^{\theta}}\leq C(\varepsilon^{2}+A^{3/2}), $$

while Lemma 6.3 gives

$$ \Bigl\|\sum_{\beta}\mathscr{E}_{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}\Bigr\|_{C^{\theta}}+\Bigl\|\sum_{\beta}\mathcal{G}_{\beta}\Bigr\|_{C^{\theta}}\leq C\varepsilon^{2}+C\varepsilon\max_{\beta}\|h_{\beta}\|_{C^{2,\theta}},\qquad\Bigl\|\sum_{\beta}\xi_{\beta}\Bigr\|_{C^{\theta}}\leq C\varepsilon^{2}. $$

Together with (8.19)-(8.20), these estimates prove (8.16).

We next estimate the five expressions in (8.15). The commutator estimate (4.71) gives

$$ \|[\Delta_{\alpha,0},\partial_{y_{i}}]\phi\|_{C^{0}}\leq C\varepsilon\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}. $$

The closest-sheet estimate and Taylor expansion give

$$ \|W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha})\|_{C^{0}}\leq CA(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{1/2}+C\varepsilon^{2}. $$

In

$$ W^{\prime\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{*})\phi\sum_{\beta}(-1)^{\beta}\mathbb{H}_{\beta}^{\prime}\Bigl(\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\beta}-\sum_{j}(h_{\beta,j}\circ\Pi_{\beta})\partial_{y_{i}}\Pi_{\beta}^{j}\Bigr), $$

the $\beta=\alpha$ summand in parentheses is $-h_{\alpha,i}$ , so the corresponding heteroclinic factor is $-\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}h_{\alpha,i}$ . The sum over $\beta\neq\alpha$ is controlled by separation and, when both sheets lie in the logarithmic strip, Proposition 4.26. Thus this expression is bounded by $C(\varepsilon^{2}+A^{3/2}+\varepsilon^{1/6}A)$ . Moreover,

$$ |\partial_{y_{i}}\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}-\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha,i}|\leq C\varepsilon\bigl(|\nabla_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}|+|\nabla^{2}_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha}|\bigr) $$

by (4.71), while $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}h_{\alpha,i}(H_{\alpha}(y,0)+\Delta_{\alpha,0}h_{\alpha})$ is bounded by the product of the two corresponding norms in (8.19). This proves (8.17).

It remains to differentiate $\mathcal{I}_{1}$ . On $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}^{0}$ , the expansion used in the proof of Lemma 6.2 is

$$ \mathcal{I}_{1}=\bigl(W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha})-1\bigr)\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}\bigl(\mathbb{H}_{\beta}-\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha-\beta)(-1)^{\beta}\bigr)+O\Bigl(\bigl(\sum_{\beta\neq\alpha}e^{-|t_{\beta}|}\bigr)^{2}\Bigr). $$

If $\partial_{y_{i}}$ hits $h_{\alpha}$ , $h_{\beta}$ , or the quadratic remainder, the result is bounded by $CA(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)(\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x))$ . If it hits $t_{\beta}$ or $\Pi_{\beta}$ , Proposition 4.26 gives $C\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)$ ; the part outside the common logarithmic strip is $O(\varepsilon^{2})$ . This proves (8.18). This is the analogue of the interaction differentiation in [29, Section 7]. ∎

On $|t_{\alpha}|<10|\log\varepsilon|$ , use Corollary 7.12 in (8.14). On its complement in the fixed $K|\log\varepsilon|$ strip, the factors $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime}$ and $\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}$ , and so do both terms in (7.47). Hence the same substitution is valid throughout the strip. Define, for the fixed index $i$ ,

$$ \widetilde{E}_{\alpha}^{\circ}=\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,1,i}, $$

$$ E^{i,\circ}=E^{i}+\partial_{y_{i}}\mathcal{I}_{1}+(-1)^{\alpha}\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,2,i}. $$

Then

$$ (\Delta_{\alpha,0}+\partial_{zz}-W^{\prime\prime}(\mathbb{H}_{\alpha}))\phi_{y_{i}}=\partial_{y_{i}}\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}^{\circ}+E^{i,\circ}, $$

Since $0<A\leq 1$ , Lemma 8.6 and (7.48) imply

$$ \displaystyle\|\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}^{\circ}\|_{C^{\theta}}+\|E^{i,\circ}\|_{C^{0}}\lesssim\; \displaystyle\varepsilon^{2}+A(r+140|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)^{3/2} \displaystyle+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+140|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x). $$

The $20|\log\varepsilon|^{2}$ increase absorbs the displacement between the ambient point and the base points used in (7.48).

We record two points needed in both the inner and outer estimates. First, at a point written in the $\alpha$ -coordinates and then in the $\beta$ -coordinates,

$$ \phi_{y_{i}}(y,z)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(\partial_{y_{i}}\Pi_{\beta}^{j})(y,z)\phi_{y_{j}}(\Pi_{\beta}(y,z),t_{\beta}(y,z))+(\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\beta})(y,z)\partial_{z}\phi(\Pi_{\beta}(y,z),t_{\beta}(y,z)). $$

Fix a ball $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ on which $|t_{\alpha}|+|t_{\beta}|\leq C|\log\varepsilon|$ . Then, on $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ , Proposition 4.26 and the higher derivative bounds in Lemma 4.11 give $\|\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\beta}\|_{C^{1,\theta}}\leq C\varepsilon^{1/6}$ , while $\|D\Pi_{\beta}\|_{C^{1,\theta}}\leq C$ . Proposition 7.1 therefore gives

$$ C\|\partial_{y_{i}}t_{\beta}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{1}^{+}(p))}\|\phi\|_{C^{2,\theta}(B_{2}^{+}(p))}\leq C\bigl(\varepsilon^{2}+\varepsilon^{1/6}A(r+120|\log\varepsilon|^{2};x)\bigr). $$

For each centre $p$ , choose $\beta$ with $p\in\mathcal{M}_{\beta}^{0}$ and keep this $\beta$ in (8.25) on all of $B_{1}^{+}(p)$ .

Second, with $\lambda_{\alpha}(y,0)$ denoting the volume density of $g_{\alpha,0}$ ,

$$ \lambda_{\alpha}(y,0)\partial_{y_{i}}\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}^{\circ}=\partial_{y_{i}}\bigl(\lambda_{\alpha}(y,0)\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}^{\circ}\bigr)-(\partial_{y_{i}}\lambda_{\alpha}(y,0))\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}^{\circ}. $$

For $i\geq 2$ , the flux in (8.27) is tangent to $y_{1}=0$ . Apply Proposition E.1(a) in the interior, (b) for $i=1$ at the boundary, and (c) for $i\geq 2$ , with the traces in Proposition 8.4. These estimates use $\|E^{i,\circ}\|_{C^{0}}$ and $\|\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}^{\circ}\|_{C^{\theta}}$ , not a norm of $\partial_{y_{i}}\widetilde{E}_{\alpha}^{\circ}$ .

#### 8.2. Improved horizontal outer estimates

Let $\Omega_{\alpha}^{2}$ be the outer region in (7.9).

#### Lemma 8.7 (Outer localization).

Fix $\rho>1$ , and then take $L>8\rho$ . For every $p\in B_{r}^{+}(x)\cap\Omega_{\alpha}^{2}\cap\{|t_{\alpha}|\leq K|\log\varepsilon|\}$ ,

for $(\Delta_{\alpha,0}+\partial_{zz}-1)\mathsf{u}=\mathsf{f}+\partial_{y_{i}}\mathsf{G}^{i}$ . For $i\geq 2$ , the last norm in (8.30) is replaced by $\|\partial_{y_{1}}\mathsf{u}\|_{C^{\theta}}$ . $$ C_{\ast}(\rho^{-1}+L^{-1})\|\phi_{y_{i}}\|_{C^{1,\theta}(B_{C_{\ast}\rho}^{\alpha}(y)\times[-2L,2L])}. $$

and hence by the expression in (8.34), since $A^{2}\leq A^{3/2}$ . 1\leq j\leq n\end{subarray}}\sup_{\begin{subarray}{c}q\in B_{r+12|\log\varepsilon|}^{+}(x)\cap\mathcal{M}_{\beta}^{0}\\
